headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API egress and secret handling can leak MinerU-processed documents; shared MCP/file pathways also create prompt-injection and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP Server and processes untrusted PDFs/DOCX/XLSX, while RD-Agent can run browsers and consume external research inputs. If MinerU output is bridged into RD-Agent through MCP or copied files, attacker-controlled document text can be treated as instructions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are passed into RD-Agent via MCP or copied files
IF RD-Agent parses document text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the two agents
Strip instruction-like text from MinerU outputs before handoff
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent messages
Review a sample document for prompt-like payloads
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred fields

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and RD-Agent requests multiple API keys and sends work to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs. If sensitive documents are processed by MinerU and then forwarded to RD-Agent, RD-Agent’s broad egress can exfiltrate that content to third parties. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs contain confidential documents or OCR text
IF RD-Agent forwards those outputs to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of the shared workflow
Block outbound API calls for the RD-Agent instance
Redact secrets and identifiers before handoff
Separate storage for MinerU outputs and RD-Agent inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU can read local files and use an MCP server; RD-Agent has broad network egress and browser access. Even without write access, both can act concurrently on shared research artifacts or logs, creating overlapping mutable-state risk if the orchestrator places them in the same workspace. The profiles do not prove locking, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory
IF the orchestrator does not provide file-level or task-level locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for MinerU inputs
Keep RD-Agent logs in a distinct path
requires-engineering: add concurrency locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU extracts structured text from documents, and RD-Agent is a research automation agent that can act on inputs via APIs and browsers. If RD-Agent treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors or hallucinated OCR can cascade into downstream actions or reports. Because the profiles show no verification gate, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes MinerU output without independent verification
IF RD-Agent uses that output to generate reports, code, or API actions
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions
Compare extracted facts against source documents
Add confidence thresholds for MinerU fields
Log provenance for every transferred datum
requires-engineering: insert a verification step between agents

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU processes document classes that can include regulated content, while RD-Agent explicitly handles secrets and sends data to third-party APIs. If regulated documents or secrets flow from MinerU into RD-Agent, the pair can create a compliance breach through external API transmission. The profiles do not show residency or DPA safeguards, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU processes regulated documents such as PHI, financial records, or personal data
IF RD-Agent transmits those materials to third-party model APIs without a DPA or residency control
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent prompts
Use a compliant local model for sensitive runs
Disable retention on external API providers where possible
Document data-class handling rules for both agents
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
